title: Fail shard if STARTED after master failover

timeline.message:
Fail shard if STARTED after master failover

If `cluster.no_master_block: all` then we remove all shards locally
whenever there's no master, but there might still be a shard-started
message in flight. When the new master is elected we start to recover
our shards again and the stale shard-started message could arrive and
move this shard to `STARTED` in the cluster state too soon. This is
pretty rare so we fix it by just failing the shard and starting the
recovery again.

Closes #87367
timeline.author: David Turner

timeline.body: Hi @DaveCTurner, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

I think this can only happen when the shard is a replica, since if it was or is now a primary, we would be in a new primary term, which would make the shard started message be skipped by the master. Can we assert that?

reply.body: Yes it looks like this can only affect replicas. I added a comment and assertion to that effect in [08cd9bb](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/87451/commits/08cd9bbb790b4ba50d67ab92cf1a795c6c0c0245).

timeline.body: I think I would prefer to depart from removing shards when no-master blocks all and instead focus on the search/fieldcaps shard level actions. But this seems to be a reasonable stop-gap solution to me.

+[[increase-tier-capacity]]
+== Not enough nodes to allocate all shard replicas
+
+Distributing copies of the data (index shard replicas) on different nodes can 
+parallelize processing requests thus speeding up search queries. This can be 
+achieved by increasing the number of replica shards up to the maximum value
+(total number of nodes minus one) which also serves the purpose to protect
+against hardware failure. If the index has a preferred tier, Elasticsearch will
+only place the copies of the data for that index on nodes in the target tier.
+
+If a warning is encountered with not enough nodes to allocate all shard 
+replicas, you can influence this behavior by adding more nodes to the cluster
+(or tier if tiers are in use), or by reducing the
+<<dynamic-index-number-of-replicas,`index.number_of_replicas`>> index setting.
+
